subject: DPA amendment: transfer gating, subprocessors, and no-adapt commitment
messages:
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@alphamed.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@alphamed.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial DPA asks — transfers, subprocessors, and training opt-out

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking the meeting last week. Legal has a short list of asks to get our procurement and privacy teams comfortable:

1) A current, signed list of subprocessors and the commitment that AlphaMed will be notified 10 days prior to any new subprocessor onboarding (we typically require 10 business days).
2) Clear language in the DPA that customer-provided content will not be used to improve public or internal models (we call this a no-adapt/no-training commitment), plus an operational playbook for how you enforce it.
3) Evidence of how data crossing EU borders is handled — KMS residency options, onshore routing, and any planned transfers to US-based analytics.
4) If you can provide a short ops/evidence pack (attestations, audit log samples, and a SOC snapshot) that would help accelerate review.

I've attached a markup of our preferred DPA language (DataProcessingAddendum_v1.docx) with inline comments. Can you confirm whether the items above are acceptable and what evidence you can share?

Thanks,
Samantha Lowe
Principal Counsel, AlphaMed Health
[Attachment: DataProcessingAddendum_v1.docx]

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@alphamed.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA asks — transfers, subprocessors, and training opt-out

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and the markup. High-level answers below, followed by next steps.

Quick answers:
- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date CSV and commit to 10 business days advance notice before adding a new subprocessor. See attached current list (subprocessor_list_20271130.csv).
- No-adapt commitment: we will add explicit DPA language that customer content will not be used to improve or fine-tune models unless the customer opts in. Operationally, we enforce this via a tenant-level flag ("no_adapt") at the routing layer and immutable audit logs.
- Cross-border handling: we offer an EU-residency lane (EU-only serving + EU KMS) for regulated customers; we can also provide a diagram of routing and transfer controls.
- Evidence pack: attaching a condensed ops runbook with attestation templates and the types of logs we can produce; for SOC evidence we can provide a recent snapshot on request (SOC snapshot request.pdf).

Attachments: subprocessor_list_20271130.csv, ops_runbook_redwood.pdf

Operational notes (what we'd need to finalize language):
- Legal: proposed DPA clause text we suggest adding (we'll paste below) — happy to accept your edits.
- Security/Ops: agree to provide an initial evidence bundle for the procurement review and a recurring delivery cadence for updated attestations.

Proposed clause (short form):
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Data to train or improve models used in production or released outside the Customer environment unless Customer provides an explicit opt-in in writing. Redwood will provide signed attestation of subprocessor controls and will provide 10 business days' notice prior to onboarding any new subprocessor impacting Customer Data."

Next steps:
1) Legal: would you prefer us to redline your attached DPA or submit a draft addendum incorporating the points above?
2) Ops: Karthik/Marissa — can you assemble the evidence pack (attestation template + sample audit log + KMS residency confirmation) by EOD Friday?

— Grace Occonnor
Head of Privacy & Policy, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessor_list_20271130.csv][Attachment: ops_runbook_redwood.pdf]

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: AlphaMed evidence pack + DPA language (action items)

Karthik / Marissa — looping you in to prepare the deliverables for AlphaMed (deal AM-2027-091). Summary and asks from legal:

What to prepare by EOD Friday (2027-12-03):
- Subprocessor attestation: signed PDF listing current subprocessors, location, and contractual access restrictions. Use the company template in /templates/attestation.
- Sample audit log: redact PII but include an example of an immutable write showing the tenant "no_adapt" flag being set and an access event from the routing layer.
- KMS residency confirmation: ops note confirming EU KMS option + steps to enable. Include SLA for onshore routing if customer requests.
- SOC evidence: prepare the SOC snapshot request that we will provide on secure Share (customer asked for a snapshot, not the full report).

Notes: we must not promise anything beyond our standard controls. For the DPA clause, legal recommended accepting Samantha's 10 business day notice but we should clarify that emergency onboarding (security fixes) can be immediate with notice after the fact. Draft a brief exception paragraph.

Marissa — can you own the attestation and sample logs? Karthik — can you draft the KMS/residency language and the limited exception paragraph? I'll take the redline for the DPA and coordinate the DocuSign.

Thanks — Grace

From: Samantha Lowe <samantha.lowe@alphamed.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@alphamed.com
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2027 14:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA amendment: transfer gating, subprocessors, and no-adapt commitment

Grace — appreciate the fast turnaround and the attachments. Legal reviewed the suggested clause and the ops pack looks good. A couple of final requests before we sign:

- Please add the 10-business-day advance notice into the DPA redline (we can accept emergency exceptions with post-notice as you suggested).
- We also ask for a process commitment: when a subprocessor change occurs we get an automated alert + a link to the updated CSV in Drive.
- For SOC evidence, AlphaMed is comfortable with a time-boxed SOC snapshot (most recent quarter) delivered via secure link; we do not need the full report.

If you can send a DocuSign-ready addendum with those three small edits, we'll run it through procurement and aim to countersign next week.

Thanks again — Samantha
Principal Counsel, AlphaMed Health
[Attachment: soc_snapshot_request.pdf]
